_comment: Motif vocabulary for prompts/linkedin_image_prompt.md, downloaded by LinkedIn Image Creator and injected as the prompt's SUBJECT_MOTIFS placeholder. It exists because the art director kept picking domain-free tension objects (handcuffs, icebergs, houses of cards) that stopped the scroll but said nothing about AI, data or automation. ART_DIRECTION decides how the image is rendered; this file decides what is in it.
_comment_no_placeholders: Never write a doubled-curly-brace placeholder anywhere in this file, not even inside a comment. DownloadTemplate scans the whole downloaded text for them and routes to stop_and_error for any name it was not passed, and this file is fetched with an empty template_vars - so one such mention in a comment kills every image run.
_comment_scoring: parse_image_motifs scores the post text against each domain's keywords (whole-word, case-insensitive, one point per distinct keyword matched) and injects the winning block. Keep keywords literal - they must be words that actually appear in a post, not concepts.
_comment_runner_up_ratio: A domain joins the winner when it scores at least this fraction of the top score. It is a ratio and not a fixed margin because a post is routinely two domains at once with very different weights: the reference post scored data-engineering 7 (its material) against career-craft 4 and automation 4 (its tension), and a margin of 1 would have thrown away exactly the anchors that fix the image.
_comment_caps: Caps applied after merging the selected domains. A small text model dilutes with a long list, so the block stays short on purpose.
_comment_domains: anchors = concrete physical things the post's SUBJECT can be rendered as. motifs = example fusions of a tension metaphor with an anchor; they are the few-shot that teaches the required degree of fusion, so every one must show the domain in its material or its form. avoid = clichés that read as stock AI/tech imagery.

career-craft._comment_avoid_museum_case: The museum case led two consecutive generated images, once lifted almost verbatim from motif 1. It is a good device that the model reaches for far too readily, so it is retired rather than fixed.

default._comment: Used when no domain clears min_score. Still automation-inflected: machined parts, control surfaces and production lines, never free-floating abstraction.

_comment_universal_avoid: Appended to every domain's avoid list. These are the failures that survive any subject: they are what the image collapses to when the model gives up on the metaphor.
universal_avoid: stock-photo scenes of people at laptops, handshakes, or teams pointing at screens
collages of technology logos or app icons
dense fake dashboards, charts and tiny unreadable labels
any composition with more than one focal point
workshop or factory scenes that read as handmade-versus-mass-production with no software texture anywhere in the lit part of the frame
_comment_rotation: parse_image_motifs shuffles each domain's anchors and motifs before round-robin selection, so consecutive posts in the same domain see different examples. The reference post reproduced career-craft motif 1 almost verbatim off a pool of three; a wider pool plus per-run rotation is what stops the four injected fusions from becoming the whole feed.
